case.vehicle: 2018-2020 compact crossover, 2.0L turbo I4, gasoline direct injection, PCM with a shared 5V sensor-reference bus, return-ground low-side switching, and CAN-linked throttle control
case.concern: Customer reports intermittent reduced-power mode after hot soak and rough idle on takeoff. MIL on. Concern began after a recent front-engine accessory belt service. No drivability issue at cruise, but tip-in is weak and the idle occasionally hunts for 5-10 seconds after restart.
case.codes:
Stored DTCs:
- P0107: Manifold Absolute Pressure/Barometric Pressure Circuit Low Input
- P0122: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit Low Input
Pending DTCs:
- P0651: Sensor Reference Voltage B Circuit/Open
Freeze-frame at key-on engine-running after stall: 5.0% throttle, 29 kPa MAP, 0.18 V MAP signal, 0.21 V TPS signal, 11.9 V system voltage.
case.findings:
Initial inspection:
- No vacuum leaks, intake duct intact, connector locks engaged, no water intrusion visible.
- Measured with DVOM back-probed to sensor ground at battery negative.
- MAP connector: 0.16 V signal, 0.00 V on 5V ref pin, ground drop 0.04 V under KOER.
- TPS connector: 0.19 V signal, 0.00 V on 5V ref pin, ground drop 0.03 V under KOER.
- PCM connector at the same reference output pin: 4.98 V key on, 4.92 V under a 150 ohm test load to battery negative.
- Harness resistance from PCM 5V output pin to the sensor branch feed pin: 0.3 ohm.
- At this point the fault could still be a shorted sensor, an opened branch, or an intermittent harness issue, because the PCM side is normal but the downstream branch is not.
case.additional:
Wednesday additional findings:
- Unplugged MAP and TPS one at a time: the branch 5V remained near 0.0 V with both sensors disconnected.
- Added a 100 ohm load from the branch 5V feed to battery negative: voltage stayed at 0.02-0.05 V at the branch, while the PCM output still held 4.9 V at its pin.
- With the engine idling and the harness flexed near the rear of the cylinder head, the branch resistance to ground changed from 8 ohm to 2 ohm.
- Voltage drop check on the 5V feed between PCM pin and the first branch splice showed 0.03 V. The drop from the splice to the sensor branch rose to 4.8 V.
- This discriminates the fault to the harness or splice downstream of the PCM, not to either sensor and not to the PCM output itself.
Friday diagnosis:
- Removed the loom tape at the harness bend behind the alternator bracket and found the 5V reference conductor chafed through to the metal bracket, with intermittent contact to ground.
- Continuity from PCM pin to the splice was intact; continuity from the splice to the sensor branch opened/shorted when the harness was moved.
- Repair performed by replacing the damaged section of wire, adding heat-shrink, and re-routing the loom away from the bracket edge.
case.root_cause: Chafed 5V reference wire in the engine harness between the PCM-side feed and the sensor branch splice, intermittently shorting to ground behind the alternator bracket.
case.diagnosis: The first test showed normal PCM reference output and zero volts at both affected sensors, which kept several possibilities open. The key discriminating step was isolating the branch with both sensors unplugged and loading the circuit: the PCM still produced a stable 5V, but the downstream branch stayed near ground and changed with harness movement. That proves the PCM was not the source of the low reference. A continuity and wiggle test then showed the fault lived in the harness after the splice. Opening the loom at the harness bend revealed the actual damage: the 5V conductor had rubbed through to the bracket and intermittently grounded the shared reference bus. Because the MAP and TPS both relied on that same branch, both codes were explained by one wiring fault rather than by two failed sensors.
case.resolution: Repaired the chafed conductor, insulated the splice, secured the harness with added clearance from the bracket, cleared codes, and repeated the failing test. Post-repair values: PCM 5V output 4.97 V, branch 5V 4.95 V, MAP signal 1.02 V KOER, TPS signal 0.68 V closed throttle, no voltage drop abnormality under a 100 ohm load, and no code return after idle, snap-throttle, and a 20-minute road test.
case.takeaway: A shared 5V bus can make two sensors look bad when the real fault is a single harness short. Measure the PCM side and the branch side under load, then wiggle-test the section between them before condemning any sensor.
